name: Basque Country, Asturias + Picos de Europa
tagline: Guggenheim and pintxos, pre-Romanesque Oviedo, Altamira, and limestone peaks an hour from a cool Atlantic coast.

access.route: Train: Brussels→Paris (1.5 h), TGV Paris→Hendaye/San Sebastián (5 h), then bus or train along the coast
Portsmouth/Plymouth→Santander or Bilbao by Brittany Ferries (24 h), or Eurostar + TGV

nightsNote: 10–13°C at the Picos huts, 16°C on the coast
whyNotes: Spain again after Seville and Córdoba, but the opposite Spain: green, cool, Atlantic, and 23°C in late July. No flights at all, and the mountains are serious without ever going high.
fitNotes: Excellent on all three of Mom's limits: highest point 2,400 m, coast at 23–26°C, and the crowds are confined to San Sebastián in August and the Cares gorge at midday. Short hops between stops.

Monte Urgull and Monte Igueldo walks
Pintxos crawl in the Parte Vieja
Chillida Leku sculpture park (20 min out)
blocks.note: Arrival point from the train. Busy in August; two nights midweek is right.

see: Guggenheim (book a morning slot)

blocks.note: The Cares path is the busiest walk in the Picos: start at 8 am.

blocks.note: Cool at altitude, 18°C days, cloud can roll in from the sea. Huts book out by spring.

see: Liencres dunes and pine forest

notes: The coast is 23–26°C, the Picos 18–22°C; Atlantic cloud some mornings, rarely all day.
Picos huts and the Fuente Dé cable car at full service; Covadonga lakes road closed to cars (shuttle).
Second half of July is the quieter half of the summer on this coast.
August: San Sebastián and the Cantabrian beaches fill with Spanish holidaymakers; the mountains do not.

lodgingAssumption: Local B&B or Airbnb, two rooms for five, one meal out a day; shared van or hire car
